newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian health sector said paralyzed by strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombian health sector said paralyzed by strike.

text.p: An estimated 120,000 Colombian doctors, nurses and health workers went on strike on Tuesday, virtually paralysing hospitals and health centres across the country, labour leaders said.
The strikers stopped all but emergency treatment to protest against the government's failure to fulfil the terms of a wage deal reached after a nationwide stoppage by state workers in February.
A Health Ministry spokesman said there was no money to meet the health workers' demands and no talks had been scheduled.
"This strike has been brought about by the government's failure once again to fulfil the terms of an agreement," Pedro Contreras, chairman of the Medical Union (ASMEDAS), told Reuters.
"We're not only fighting for wages but believe the government wants to reduce public health care while the majority of Colombians do not have the means to buy (private) health care," he said.

He said the strike had hit more than 6,500 health centres and 640 hospitals. Emergency services and childbirth facilities were being maintained but routine appointments and pre-scheduled operations had been cancelled, Contreras said.

Under the February deal, the government agreed to give wage hikes of about 20 percent to all state workers. State health workers should have received an additional payment, backdated to Jan. 1, to bring their pay into line with other professions.
Health Ministry sources said the ministry would now have to appeal to Congress for an additional budget allocation.
